description: 5 should-trigger + 5 should-not-trigger queries for the component-shape decision. Should-trigger covers the five shapes this skill decides — splitting an over-loaded component, the composition-vs-inheritance call, a slot/children contract, the controlled-vs-uncontrolled axis, and where a new component belongs under a project's own granularity taxonomy (§ Read state.ui_audit.component_taxonomy). Should-not-trigger covers the near misses whose vocabulary overlaps hardest: styling a component that already exists, auditing what the project owns (that is existing-ui-audit, which runs first and feeds this one), a backend shape question that borrows the same composition words, a one-line prop rename, and general React knowledge with no component to shape.

queries.q: this Table component has grown to 19 props — how should I split it?
should the Dialog share behaviour by composition or by extending a base class?
design the slot contract for our Card so consumers can replace the header
should this Combobox be controlled or uncontrolled, and what is the prop API?
we organize components as primitives/patterns/features — where does a new Checkout shell belong?
make the primary button's hover state a bit darker
inventory which components this project already owns before we build anything
should this service compose its collaborators or extend an abstract base repository?
rename the isOpen prop to open across the codebase
explain when React re-renders a memoized child
